title: Dense-open localization
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $C$ be a reduced separated scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim C\le1$ (a reduced curve, as in [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]). Let $r$ be a prime number and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $C_{\Et}$, i.e. an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] with $rF=0$, which is constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]; in particular $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair. Then:

1. There is a dense open subscheme $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ which is a finite disjoint union $U=\coprod_{a=1}^nU_a$ of irreducible open subschemes $U_a$ (each a reduced irreducible separated $k$-scheme of finite type of dimension $\le1$), such that $j^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant].
2. The closed complement $Z=C\setminus U$, with its reduced induced structure and closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], is zero-dimensional (a finite, possibly empty, set of closed points), and the sequence
$$
 0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0
$$
of extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and inverse image, whose maps are the counit of $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and the unit of $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$, is exact.
3. Let $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow C$ be the composite open immersion. Then
$$
 \mathcal C(C,F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C(C,j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))\text{ for every }a,
$$
where, for a curve coefficient pair $(C,G)$, $\mathcal C(C,G)$ is the conjunction of the eight assertions $\mathcal C_1(C,G),\dots,\mathcal C_8(C,G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], each an implication that is true when its hypotheses (on $C$: affine, proper; on $G$: constructible, prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, $p$-primary) fail, as in Stacks, Situation 0A52.

proof.text: Apply the existing generic-constancy theorem to obtain a dense open V on which F is finite locally constant. Shrink V by the proved dense irreducible-opens theorem. This yields finitely many disjoint irreducible opens U_a, their dense union W, zero-dimensional complement, and irreducible connected components in W. Finite local constancy of each restriction and of the restriction to W follows from upperStar_of_range_subset because U_a and W lie inside V.
Apply the dense-open prime-coefficient assertion equivalence to W to identify assertions for F with those for extension by zero of its restriction to W.

Compose the preceding equivalence with the finite-disjoint-open assertion equivalence. Together with the geometric data and restriction witnesses this gives the required existential componentwise conclusion.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $C$ be a reduced curve over an algebraically closed field $k$, let
$\Lambda$ be a finite ring, $r$ a prime, and $F$ a constructible sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $C_{\Et}$ with $rF=0$. There are finitely many pairwise
disjoint irreducible opens $U_1,\dots,U_m\subseteq C$ whose union $U$ is
dense, whose complement $Z=C\setminus U$ is zero-dimensional, and on each of
which $F$ is finite locally constant, such that, writing
$j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow C$ for the inclusions,

$$
 \mathcal C(C,F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C(C,j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a}))\text{ for every }a,
$$

where $\mathcal C$ denotes the eight assertions of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

proof.text:
The finite partition of $C$ into locally closed constructible subschemes on
which the constructible sheaf $F$ is lisse (locally constant with
finite stalks) is a stratification in the sense of
[def-constructible-stratification] whose pullbacks of $F$ are finite locally
constant, so $F$ is constructible in the sense of
[def-constructible-constructible]. By [prop-constructible-generic-constancy]
there is a dense open $U'\subseteq C$ with $F|_{U'}$ finite locally constant.
Remove from $U'$ the finitely many closed points at which two distinct
irreducible components of $C$ meet; the result is a dense open
$j:U\hookrightarrow C$ on which $F$ is still finite locally constant, a reduced
curve whose irreducible components are disjoint, hence a finite disjoint union
$U=\coprod_aU_a$ of irreducible curves. Its complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$
contains no generic point of $C$, so it is zero-dimensional. The natural
sequence $0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ is exact, since at geometric points
of $U$ the middle and left terms agree and the right term vanishes, and at
geometric points of $Z$ the left term vanishes and the sequence is the
identity of the right term. For the equivalence: $j_!j^{-1}F$ decomposes as
the finite direct sum of the $j_{a,!}(F|_{U_a})$ (the $U_a$ are open and
closed in $U$), the terms $i_*i^{-1}F$ are constructible on the
zero-dimensional $Z$, where all $\mathcal C_j$
([def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]) hold: the vanishing and
finite-stalk finiteness statements follow from
[lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology], field-extension invariance follows
from [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension], and (C8) is a map
between zero groups. Moreover, $\mathcal C(-,G_1\oplus G_2)$ is equivalent to
$\mathcal C(-,G_1)\wedge\mathcal C(-,G_2)$ for the finite direct sums;
together with [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] this gives the
implication from right to left. For the converse, $H^q(C,i_*i^{-1}F)=0$ for
$q>0$ and $H^0(C,i_*i^{-1}F)$ is the finite product of the stalks of $F$ at
the points of $Z$, unchanged under algebraically closed extension; so the long
exact sequence gives $H^q(C,j_!j^{-1}F)\cong H^q(C,F)$ for $q\geq2$ and a
five-term exact sequence in degrees $0,1$, compatible with restriction to
opens and with field extension, and each assertion for $j_!j^{-1}F$ follows
from the one for $F$ by the five lemma, as in the proof of
[lemma-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-reduction].
